stem: When did Non-Cooperation movement start on the question of the caliphate?
expl: A special session of the Congress was held under the leadership of Lala Lajpat Rai in Calcutta in September, 1920 AD to decide upon the momentous issue of Non-Cooperation. Discussions were held on the Khilafat question, the Government’s failure to protect the innocent people of the Punjab and punish the British offi cers. The leaders decided that the only way to vindicate the national honour was to establish Swaraj through the policy of Non-Cooperation. The resolution of non-cooperation movement was formally adopted in this session. The resolution of the Calcutta Congress was ratifi ed at the regular session held in Nagpur in December, 1920 AD.

stem: Which one of the following was not a cause for starting the Non-Cooperation Movement?
expl: The Non-Cooperation Movement was a signifi cant but short phase of the Indian independence movement from the British rule. It was led by Mahatma Gandhi after the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre and lasted from 1920 A.D. to February 1922 A.D. The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched on 1 August 1920 A.D. and withdrawn in February 1922 A.D. after the Chauri Chaura incident. The factors leading to this movement were Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh massacre and question of Khilafat. The salt march, also known as the Dandi March, lasted from 12th March 1930 A.D. to 6 April 1930 A.D.

stem: Who was the President of the special session of Indian National Congress held in Calcutta in September, 1920 in which the resolution of Non-cooperation Movement was passed?
expl: The Special session of the Indian National Congress was held at Calcutta in September, 1920 A.D. under the presidency of Lala Lajpat Rai. Instigated by the British Governments attitude towards the Khilafat movement and the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, a special session was organized specifi cally to pass the resolution of the Non-Cooperation Movement with a demand for Swaraj. It was attended by most of the national leaders of the freedom struggle at the time and almost 300 other delegates from Bihar. The resolution was passed with a great majority. Under the resolution, people were advised to resign from administrative bodies and give up honorary titles, withdraw children from Government Schools and College, refuse to attend offi cials events by the Government; boycott British courts and foreign goods and adopt Swadeshi goods and garments. Gandhi predicted that Swaraj would be attained in a year if the Non-cooperation movement was successful. The movement created ripples within the nation and provided the impetus to the nationalist movement.

expl: On 4th February, 1922 A.D., the angry residents of Chauri-Chaura village gathered in front of the police station to protest against the arrest of their leader, while campaigning against the sale of liquor. The working committee of the Congress met in February, 1922 A.D. and decided to withdraw the Movement and urged the party workers to get involved in constructive works, such as popularizing khadi, establishing National schools and working towards Hindu-Muslim unity. stem:
Consider the following subjects with regard to Non-Cooperation Programme :
I. Boycott of law-courts and foreign cloth
II. Observance of strict non-violence
III. Retention of titles and honours without using them in public
IV. Establishment of Panchayats for settling disputes How many of the above were parts of Non-Cooperation Programme?
expl: The Non-Cooperation Programme was officially accepted by the Indian National Congress at the Calcutta Special Session in 1920 and then at the Nagpur Session in December 1920. The Non-Cooperation Programme accepted at the Nagpur Session included the following points – Renunciation of titles and honours; Boycott of law courts and foreign cloth; Establishment of panchayats to settle disputes; and the expectation that people strictly adhere to non-violence. The Congress and Gandhiji had called for a complete renunciation of the titles and honours given by the British government; there was no question of keeping them while merely avoiding their public use. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect. Hence, three out of the four statements are correct, and the correct option is (c).
